subject: Human Evolution
title: Underground Storage Organs
description: A quick win: understand Underground Storage Organs.

hook.text: When drought kills the grass, tubers underground still hold calories. Dig, and you survive.

buildup.text: Tubers, corms, and bulbs are rich in starch—packed energy that surface plants lack during dry seasons.

discovery.text: Digging sticks—simple pointed branches—opened a calorie vault no other primate could access.

twist.text: Raw tubers are tough to digest. Cooking made them two to three times more nutritious.

climax.text: Underground foods may have been the key fallback that kept hominins alive between big kills.

punchline.text: Survival was buried a few inches below the surface.

quiz.question: Why were underground storage organs important for early hominins?
options: They provided reliable calories during dry seasons
They were easy to digest raw
